properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 8:35AM EDT until October 5 at 10:30AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Franklin County in Big Bend Florida...
Southeastern Gulf County in the panhandle of Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM EDT /930 AM CDT/.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 835 AM EDT /735 AM CDT/, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain
due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Carrabelle, Eastpoint, Apalachicola, St George Island, Franklin,
Creels, Hays Place, Green Point, Beverly, High Bluff, Bay City,
Apalachicola Airport, Buck Siding, Royal Bluff, Tilton, St George
Island St Pk, Howard Creek, Nine Mile, Yent Place and Carrabelle
Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 5 at 8:13AM EDT until October 5 at 9:45AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 945 AM EDT/845 AM CDT/.

* At 813 AM EDT/713 AM CDT/, severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from 18
nm northeast of Mexico Beach to 11 nm west of Apalachicola to 28 nm
southwest of Empire Mica Wreck, moving northeast at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Buckeye Reef, O Tower, K Tower, S Tower, V Tower, Empire Mica
Wreck, Horseshoe Beach, Apalachicola, C Tower, St George Island,
Marker 24 Barge, and St. Marks.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 5 at 7:10AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Barataria Bay...
Coastal waters from the Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana out 20 NM...

At 710 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak waterspouts. This
thunderstorm was located near Barataria Bay, moving south at 10
knots.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves and dangerous lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe
harbor immediately until this activity passes.

Brief, weak waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on
alert in case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 6:47AM CDT until October 5 at 9:45AM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Dale County in southeastern Alabama...
Henry County in southeastern Alabama...
Clay County in southwestern Georgia...
Southern Quitman County in southwestern Georgia...
Randolph County in southwestern Georgia...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM CDT /1045 AM EDT/.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 647 AM CDT /747 AM EDT/, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain
due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 3 and 6 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Abbeville, Fort Gaines, Cuthbert, Shellman, Newville, Bellville,
Fort Gaines-Clay Airport, Days Crossroads and Standleys Store.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
